claim: Since January 2020 nearly 600 million people have been infected worldwide with the SARS-CoV-2 virus.
source: Since January 2020 nearly 600 million people have been infected worldwide with the SARS-CoV-2 virus, the vast majority of whom have developed COVID-19, the disease (A Sehgal et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to A Sehgal et al., 2021

claim: The vast majority of people infected with SARS-CoV-2 have developed COVID-19.
source: Since January 2020 nearly 600 million people have been infected worldwide with the SARS-CoV-2 virus, the vast majority of whom have developed COVID-19, the disease (A Sehgal et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to A Sehgal et al., 2021

claim: COVID-19 has resulted in nearly 6 million deaths.
source: COVID-19 has also resulted in nearly 6 million deaths, primarily as a result of pulmonary injury and its subsequent comorbidities.
evidence: Statement of epidemiological data from the pandemic

claim: COVID-19 deaths occur primarily as a result of pulmonary injury and its subsequent comorbidities.
source: COVID-19 has also resulted in nearly 6 million deaths, primarily as a result of pulmonary injury and its subsequent comorbidities.

claim: The pandemic has continued despite the availability of several vaccines and boosters.
source: Despite the availability of several vaccines and boosters, the pandemic has continued, and the cost to society continues to mount (Ahmad et al., 2020b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ahmad et al., 2020b

claim: The omicron variant in early 2022 rapidly spread across virtually every country.
source: The most recent viral variant in early 2022, omicron, rapidly spread across virtually every country, with significant morbidity and mortality, coupled with a greater degree of infectivity.
evidence: Based on epidemiological observations during the omicron wave

claim: The omicron variant had a greater degree of infectivity than previous variants.
source: The most recent viral variant in early 2022, omicron, rapidly spread across virtually every country, with significant morbidity and mortality, coupled with a greater degree of infectivity.
evidence: Based on epidemiological observations of omicron spread

claim: A significant subpopulation of patients have persistent symptoms 4 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: Although the majority of individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 recover, there is a significant subpopulation of patients with persistent symptoms 4 weeks after infection, even among those who suffered from mild-to-moderate COVID-19.

claim: Persistent symptoms occur even among those who suffered from mild-to-moderate COVID-19.
source: Although the majority of individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 recover, there is a significant subpopulation of patients with persistent symptoms 4 weeks after infection, even among those who suffered from mild-to-moderate COVID-19.
evidence: Based on clinical observations of PASC

claim: Post-COVID symptomatology includes brain fog, exertional fatigue, dyspnea, chest tightness, gastrointestinal disturbances, and vertigo.
source: Some of that symptomatology include brain fog, exertional fatigue, dyspnea, chest tightness, gastrointestinal disturbances, and vertigo (Alkodaymi et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Alkodaymi et al., 2022

claim: Post-COVID symptoms may represent prodromes to future health threats such as development of autoimmune diseases.
source: Those symptoms and their resultant clinical signs (e.g., glucose intolerance, sleep disorders, postural hypotension, and cardiac arrythmias) may also represent prodromes to future health threats (e.g., development of autoimmune diseases).
evidence: Speculative statement about potential future health consequences

claim: The demographics of individuals who suffer from post-COVID complaints are insufficient to draw conclusions about gender, age, and social determinants of health as contributing factors.
source: The demographics of individuals who suffer from these complaints are insufficient to draw conclusions about gender, age, and social determinants of health as contributing factors (Bechmann et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bechmann et al., 2022

claim: Current estimates of PASC prevalence vary widely between 12% and 50% of individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2.
source: Current estimates vary widely; somewhere between 12% and 50% of individuals who are infected with SARS-CoV-2 will likely develop post-COVID symptoms more than a month after an initial infection (Bechmann et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bechmann et al., 2022

claim: Metabolic dysfunction (obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes mellitus) is a predisposing risk factor for severe acute COVID-19.
source: Metabolic dysfunction (i.e., obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes mellitus) is a predisposing risk factor for severe acute COVID-19, and there is emerging evidence that this factor plus a chronic inflammatory state may predispose to PASC.
evidence: Based on established clinical observations and research

claim: Metabolic dysfunction plus a chronic inflammatory state may predispose to PASC.
source: Metabolic dysfunction (i.e., obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes mellitus) is a predisposing risk factor for severe acute COVID-19, and there is emerging evidence that this factor plus a chronic inflammatory state may predispose to PASC.
evidence: Based on emerging research evidence discussed in the manuscript

claim: Obesity and insulin resistance with type 2 diabetes are established risk factors for the development of severe COVID-19.
source: But it is clear these conditions are established risk factors for the development of severe COVID-19 suggesting a predisposition for enhanced viral entry into cells of the respiratory tract (Aminian et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2021; Drucker, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aminian et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2021; Drucker, 2021

claim: Obesity and insulin resistance suggest a predisposition for enhanced viral entry into cells of the respiratory tract.
source: But it is clear these conditions are established risk factors for the development of severe COVID-19 suggesting a predisposition for enhanced viral entry into cells of the respiratory tract (Aminian et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2021; Drucker, 2021).
evidence: Inference based on cited research about metabolic risk factors

claim: Mendelian randomization studies have analyzed potential causal associations linking 17 cardiometabolic risk factors, including BMI, with susceptibility to severe SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: Mendelian randomization studies have analyzed potential causal associations linking 17 cardiometabolic risk factors, including body mass index (BMI), with susceptibility to severe SARS-CoV-2 infection although confounding from T2D cannot be excluded (Leong et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Leong et al., 2020

claim: Hyperglycemia, with or without a history of diabetes, is a strong predictor of in-hospital adverse outcomes.
source: Nevertheless, hyperglycemia, with or without a history of diabetes, is a strong predictor of in-hospital adverse outcomes, portending a sevenfold higher mortality compared to patients with well-controlled blood glucose levels (Zhu et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2020

claim: Hyperglycemia portends a sevenfold higher mortality compared to patients with well-controlled blood glucose levels.
source: Nevertheless, hyperglycemia, with or without a history of diabetes, is a strong predictor of in-hospital adverse outcomes, portending a sevenfold higher mortality compared to patients with well-controlled blood glucose levels (Zhu et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2020 with specific quantitative data

claim: Individuals with higher BMI had an increased risk of COVID-19-related mortality in the UK BioBank study.
source: Analysis of COVID-19 mortality in participants from the United Kingdom (UK) BioBank showed that individuals with higher BMI, had an increased risk of COVID-19-related mortality (Peters et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Peters et al., 2020

claim: Higher BMI is strongly associated with greater risk of mortality in ICU patients infected with SARS-CoV-2.
source: This is especially pertinent for patients in the ICU infected with SARS-CoV-2, in whom higher BMI is strongly associated with greater risk of mortality (Cummings et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cummings et al., 2020

claim: Coagulopathies, endothelial dysfunction, underlying cardiovascular disease, and chronic inflammation with an impaired adaptive immune system often coexist in both T1D and T2D.
source: However, it is complicated by other associated etiologic elements that often coexist in both T1D and T2D. For example, coagulopathies, endothelial dysfunction, underlying cardiovascular disease, and chronic inflammation with an impaired adaptive immune system all can be present in a single individual and raise the risk of subsequent morbidity and mortality (Chen et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2020

claim: Hyperglycemia, chronic inflammatory markers, and T-cell dysfunction are the three predominant signs in patients with T2D.
source: Nonetheless, hyperglycemia, chronic inflammatory markers, and T-cell dysfunction remain the three predominant signs in patients with T2D and hence are also likely to be major drivers of morbidity during SARS-CoV-2 infection.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of T2D pathophysiology

claim: There remains an ongoing debate about whether ACE2 is present in islet cells.
source: There remains an ongoing debate about whether ACE2, the predominant receptor for SARS-CoV-2, is present in islet cells (Drucker, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Drucker, 2021

claim: TMPRSS2 is expressed on beta cells and in the blood vessels of the pancreas.
source: There is more evidence that one of the accessory proteins for viral binding, TMPRSS2 is expressed on beta cells, and also in the blood vessels of the pancreas.
evidence: Based on research evidence about TMPRSS2 expression

claim: The soluble form of CD26 possesses dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) activity.
source: There is some evidence that the soluble form of the surface T-cell activation antigen CD26, which possesses dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) activity, can serve as a coreceptor for SARS-CoV-2.
evidence: Based on established biochemical knowledge

claim: Soluble CD26 can serve as a coreceptor for SARS-CoV-2.
source: There is some evidence that the soluble form of the surface T-cell activation antigen CD26, which possesses dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) activity, can serve as a coreceptor for SARS-CoV-2.
evidence: Based on research evidence about CD26 function

claim: DPP-4 degrades GLPs and GLP-1 receptor agonists.
source: As an enzyme, DPP-4 degrades GLPs and GLP-1 receptor agonists, and DPP-4 inhibitors are used to treat T2D.
evidence: Based on established biochemical and pharmacological knowledge

claim: DPP-4 inhibitors are used to treat T2D.
source: As an enzyme, DPP-4 degrades GLPs and GLP-1 receptor agonists, and DPP-4 inhibitors are used to treat T2D.
evidence: Based on established clinical practice

claim: CD26 is thought to be involved in the binding of SARS-CoV-2 through its S1 recombinant receptor-binding domain.
source: Soluble DPP-4 is also an adipokine, but importantly CD26 is thought to be involved in the binding of SARS-CoV-2 through its S1 recombinant receptor-binding domain, aiding in viral entry (Lamers et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lamers et al., 2011

claim: There are little data to support the use of DPP-4 inhibition to reduce the severity of COVID-19 at present.
source: Inhibition of DPP-4 activity to reduce the severity of COVID-19 has been under investigation, but there are little data to support its use at present, either prophylactically or during infection (Solerte et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Solerte et al., 2020

claim: Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance is characterized by hyperinsulinemia as the pancreatic beta cells attempt to overcome hyperglycemia by increasing insulin secretion.
source: Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance is characterized by hyperinsulinemia as the pancreatic beta cells are still functional, but attempt to overcome hyperglycemia by increasing insulin secretion.
evidence: Based on established understanding of insulin resistance pathophysiology

claim: In a cohort of 551 patients hospitalized for COVID-19 in Italy, 46% of patients were hyperglycemic.
source: In a cohort of 551 patients hospitalized for COVID-19 in Italy, the authors found that 46% of patients were hyperglycemic, whereas 27% were normoglycemic.
evidence: Data from Italian cohort study

claim: Even normoglycemic COVID-19 patients had evidence of insulin resistance and increased cytokine levels.
source: Even normoglycemic individuals had evidence of insulin resistance and increased cytokine levels.
evidence: Data from the Italian cohort study

claim: GP73, a Golgi protein induced by infections, was increased during recent SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: Recently, Wan et al. reported that GP73, a Golgi protein induced by infections, was increased during recent SARS-CoV-2 infection (Wan et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wan et al., 2022

claim: Injection of recombinant GP73 raised blood glucose in mice within 15 min.
source: Furthermore, they showed that injection of recombinant GP73 raised blood glucose in mice within 15 min.
evidence: Experimental data from Wan et al. study

claim: Treatment of primary mouse hepatocytes with rmGP73 resulted in a dose- and time-dependent increase in glucose release.
source: To address the mechanistic basis of those findings, the authors treated primary mouse hepatocytes with rmGP73 and observed a dose- and time-dependent increase in glucose release in association with increased levels of intracellular cAMP, activation of protein kinase A (PKA) and expression of key gluconeogenic genes.
evidence: Experimental data from Wan et al. study

claim: Enhanced hepatic glucose production may be responsible for the dysglycemia of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: These data provide clues that enhanced hepatic glucose production may be responsible for the dysglycemia of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
evidence: Inference based on the GP73 experimental data

claim: Obesity is associated with a decrease in the functionality of white adipose tissue, characterized by inflammation and reduced neutral lipid storage in adipocytes.
source: The underlying metabolic dysfunction associated with obesity includes in almost every case a decrease in the functionality of white adipose tissue, characterized by inflammation and reduced neutral lipid storage in adipocytes.
evidence: Based on established understanding of obesity pathophysiology

claim: Adipose tissue dysfunction results in the deposition of lipids in other tissues and triggers immune and vascular pathology.
source: This in turn results in the deposition of lipids in other tissues and triggers immune and vascular pathology.
evidence: Based on established understanding of ectopic lipid deposition

claim: Ectopic lipid deposition is frequently associated with the generation of secondary signaling lipids, such as ceramides.
source: Ectopic deposition is frequently associated with the generation of secondary signaling lipids, such as ceramides, which are proinflammatory, proapoptotic, and confer further insulin resistance in their own right.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of lipid metabolism

claim: Ceramides are proinflammatory, proapoptotic, and confer further insulin resistance.
source: Ectopic deposition is frequently associated with the generation of secondary signaling lipids, such as ceramides, which are proinflammatory, proapoptotic, and confer further insulin resistance in their own right.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of ceramide biology

claim: Prevailing hypoxia in obese adipose tissue can lead to the activation of hypoxia-inducible factor transcription elements that can turn on profibrotic programs.
source: Prevailing hypoxia in obese adipose tissue can lead to the activation of hypoxia-inducible factor transcription elements that can turn on profibrotic programs as well.
evidence: Based on established understanding of hypoxia signaling in adipose tissue

claim: Fibrosis is a widespread phenomenon in obese adipose tissue, leading to enhanced adipocyte necrosis with associated local and subclinical systemic inflammation.
source: Fibrosis is a widespread phenomenon in obese adipose tissue, leading to enhanced adipocyte necrosis with associated local and subclinical systemic inflammation.
evidence: Based on established understanding of adipose tissue pathology in obesity

claim: Patients with obesity and T2D have slower gastric motility and increased intestinal permeability, leading to enhanced endotoxin levels in circulation.
source: Further exasperating these inflammatory conditions are slower gastric motility and increased intestinal permeability, leading to enhanced endotoxin levels in circulation.
evidence: Based on established understanding of metabolic endotoxemia

claim: Patients with obesity and T2D are frequently 'primed' with enhanced baseline inflammation.
source: Patients with obesity and T2D are frequently 'primed' with enhanced baseline inflammation.
evidence: Based on established understanding of chronic inflammation in metabolic disease

claim: Enhanced plasma endotoxin levels have vastly synergistic proinflammatory properties with viral components, particularly the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.
source: Several studies have highlighted the vastly synergistic proinflammatory properties of enhanced plasma endotoxin levels with viral components, particularly the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.
evidence: Based on multiple studies showing synergistic inflammatory effects

claim: Adipocytes and 'adipocyte-like cells' can undergo a dedifferentiation event, losing typical adipocyte markers such as PPARγ and adiponectin.
source: Finally, observations in the recent past have highlighted the ability of adipocytes and 'adipocyte-like cells' (such as the lipofibroblasts in the lung and stellate cells in the liver) to undergo a dedifferentiation event, thereby losing typical adipocyte markers, such as the master adipogenic transcription factor PPARγ, as well as one of its primary target genes, adiponectin (Sun et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sun et al., 2020

claim: In the lung, lipofibroblasts morph into myofibroblasts during SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: In the lung, lipofibroblasts morph into myofibroblasts during the infection, which in turn are likely culprits in the dramatically enhanced profibrotic environment seen during viral exposure.
evidence: Based on research about cellular changes during infection

claim: Adiponectin is reduced while leptin is enhanced during SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: In this context, the potent antifibrotic and anti-inflammatory factor adiponectin is reduced, while the proinflammatory adipokine leptin is enhanced (Elrobaa and New, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Elrobaa and New, 2021

claim: Many immune cells of the innate and adaptive immune system, including T cells, express leptin receptors.
source: Many immune cells of the innate and adaptive immune system, including T cells, express leptin receptors, and may disproportionally respond to the viral challenge.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of leptin receptor expression

claim: Stabilizing cells in their 'inactive' adipocyte-like state through activation of the PPARγ pathway may prevent the emergence of myofibroblasts.
source: Stabilizing cells in their 'inactive' adipocyte-like state through activation of the PPARγ pathway may prevent the emergence of myofibroblasts.
evidence: Speculative therapeutic proposal based on understanding of PPARγ function

claim: PPARγ is antifibrotic, anti-inflammatory, and potently upregulates adiponectin.
source: PPARγ is antifibrotic, anti-inflammatory, and potently upregulates adiponectin.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of PPARγ function

claim: Both the PPARγ and the leptin pathway offer significant potential for treatment of acute viral response and PASC.
source: Both the PPARγ and the leptin pathway offer significant potential in the future, not only in the context of the acute viral response, but also in the context of the prolonged consequences associated with PASC (Elrobaa and New, 2021; Tanowitz et al., 2017).

claim: T-cell dysfunction and aberrant cytokine production occur in T2D and obesity.
source: Recent reports suggest that T-cell dysfunction and aberrant cytokine production occur in T2D as well as obesity and may be an underlying cause of both infection severity and length of time to full recovery from SARS-CoV-2.

claim: T-cell dysfunction may be an underlying cause of both infection severity and length of time to full recovery from SARS-CoV-2.
source: Recent reports suggest that T-cell dysfunction and aberrant cytokine production occur in T2D as well as obesity and may be an underlying cause of both infection severity and length of time to full recovery from SARS-CoV-2.
evidence: Inference based on recent research

claim: IL-10 was produced in greater amounts from T cells of lean/healthy donors compared to prediabetes patients.
source: IL-10 was produced in greater amounts from cells of lean/healthy donors, and there were differences in production of Th1/Th17 cytokines, that is, more CCL-20, TNFα, GM-CSF in prediabetes, and less IL-6/-12 were noted (Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2022 with experimental data

claim: Prediabetes patients had more CCL-20, TNFα, and GM-CSF production from T cells compared to lean/healthy donors.
source: IL-10 was produced in greater amounts from cells of lean/healthy donors, and there were differences in production of Th1/Th17 cytokines, that is, more CCL-20, TNFα, GM-CSF in prediabetes, and less IL-6/-12 were noted (Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2022 with experimental data

claim: Metabolic status, independent of age, significantly shifts inflammatory profiles.
source: These data are consistent with the tenet that metabolic status, independent of age, significantly shifts inflammatory profiles.

claim: Interferons are the first line of defense with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: In respect to the innate immune response, interferons are the first line of defense with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, and are secreted following release of viral contents into the cytoplasm.

claim: The early immune response is orchestrated by airway epithelial and alveolar epithelial cells (ATII) as well as alveolar macrophages.
source: The early response is orchestrated by airway epithelial and alveolar epithelial cells (ATII) as well as alveolar macrophages.
evidence: Based on established understanding of pulmonary immune response

claim: A regulated and controlled release of cytokines and chemokines in the early phase of infection is not proinflammatory but is focused on viral clearance in the vast majority of patients.
source: A regulated and controlled release of cytokines and chemokines in the early phase of infection is not proinflammatory but is focused on viral clearance in the vast majority of patients (Song et al., 2020).

claim: In a small percent of patients, the immune response is dysfunctional and can lead to a dramatic release of cytokines and the clinical scenario of 'cytokine storm'.
source: However, in a small percent of patients, that response is dysfunctional and can lead to a dramatic release of cytokines and the clinical scenario of 'cytokine storm'.

claim: Among 30 patients with acute COVID-19, the number of circulating CD26+ cells decreased during the acute illness, particularly in those with severe disease.
source: In a recent paper, among 30 patients with acute COVID-19 of varying severity, the number of circulating CD26+ cells decreased during the acute illness, particularly in those with severe disease (deKay et al., 2021).

claim: CD26+ cells rose in patients that fully recovered but not in those with prolonged disease or death.
source: Ultimately, CD26+ cells rose in those patients that fully recovered but not in those with prolonged disease or death.

claim: CD26 cell number correlated with hospital-free days in patients with mild disease.
source: CD26 cell number correlated with hospital-free days, and in those with mild disease, indicating that in contrast to a soluble form, membrane-bound CD26 might be associated with T-cell-specific immunity against SARS-CoV 2.

claim: Membrane-bound CD26 might be associated with T-cell-specific immunity against SARS-CoV-2.
source: CD26 cell number correlated with hospital-free days, and in those with mild disease, indicating that in contrast to a soluble form, membrane-bound CD26 might be associated with T-cell-specific immunity against SARS-CoV 2.

claim: CD26+ T cells secrete high levels of IL-17, which amplifies cytokine production in patients with acute COVID-19.

claim: Lymphopenia is a common finding in moderately to severely ill COVID-19 patients.
source: Lymphopenia is a common finding in moderately to severely ill COVID-19 patients, and both circulating CD4+ andCD8+ T cells suffer exhaustion and depletion while activated T cells persist in tissues.

claim: Both circulating CD4+ and CD8+ T cells suffer exhaustion and depletion while activated T cells persist in tissues in COVID-19 patients.
source: Lymphopenia is a common finding in moderately to severely ill COVID-19 patients, and both circulating CD4+ andCD8+ T cells suffer exhaustion and depletion while activated T cells persist in tissues.

claim: The T-cell response in COVID-19 is heterogeneous.
source: However, the story is much more complex than simple depletion and other studies have suggested that the T-cell response is heterogeneous (Ahmad et al., 2020a).

claim: Gastrointestinal symptoms compared with respiratory symptoms of PASC are associated with unique T-cell clonal and transcriptional dynamics.

claim: The underlying pathophysiology of PASC is multifactorial due to the plethora of sequelae, symptomology, and extent of tissue injury.
source: It is almost certain that the underlying pathophysiology of PASC is multifactorial due to the plethora of sequelae, symptomology, and extent of tissue injury (A Sehgal et al., 2021; see Figure 1).

claim: Vaccinated individuals were far less likely to develop PASC, particularly those vaccinated within a week of their acute infection.
source: For example, a recent review of studies up to mid-January 2022 showed that vaccinated individuals were far less likely to develop PASC, particularly those vaccinated within a week of their acute infection (UK Health Security Agency, 2022).

claim: Three main symptoms stand out in the majority of PASC cases: fatigue, cough, and anosmia/dysgeusia.
source: Although there are more outstanding questions than evidence surrounding the risk and incidence of PASC, there is emerging evidence that three main symptoms stand out in the majority of cases: fatigue, cough, and anosmia/dysgeusia (Su et al., 2022).

claim: T2D has been very strongly associated with fatigue, cough, and anosmia/dysgeusia symptoms in PASC.

claim: Obesity is a major risk factor for PASC in Italian healthcare workers.

claim: T2D and high levels of acute SARS-CoV-2 RNAemia were strong predisposing risk factors for PASC.

claim: Patients with T2D who developed COVID-19 had a much greater likelihood of having high fatigue scores postinfection than controls who were not infected.

claim: In one study, the number of post-COVID symptoms was similar between diabetes and control groups (incident rate ratio 1.06, 95% CI 0.92–1.24, p = 0.372).

claim: The most prevalent post-COVID symptoms were fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and pain.
source: The most prevalent post-COVID symptoms were fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and pain.

claim: New onset diabetes was diagnosed at 1 year post-COVID-19 recovery in 7 patients (1.3%) in a longitudinal follow-up of 736 patients in Spain.
source: In a longitudinal follow-up of 736 patients with a positive COVID-19 diagnosis early in the pandemic, in Spain, new onset diabetes was diagnosed at 1 year post-COVID-19 recovery in 7 patients (1.3%).

claim: Intensification of oral antidiabetic drugs or insulin was required in 15 previously known diabetic patients at 1 year post-COVID-19 recovery.
source: In addition, intensification of oral antidiabetic drugs or insulin was required in 15 previously known diabetic patients (of which there were 189 patients).

claim: Among 551 patients without a history of diabetes and normal HbA1c, nearly half had glycemic abnormalities during acute COVID-19 illness.

claim: Glycemic abnormalities could be detected for at least 2 months in patients who recovered from COVID-19.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 can infect and persist in adipose tissue.

claim: The magnitude of plasma viral load is associated with lower absolute lymphocyte counts, increased markers of inflammation, and a worse prognosis.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 can directly infect endothelial cells.

claim: Tissue studies have revealed evidence of endothelitis with perivascular inflammation and the extrapulmonary spread of SARS-CoV-2 to other organs.

claim: The virus can be detected in feces and possibly spread through fecal contamination.

claim: Gastrointestinal symptoms persist in PASC.

claim: There is significant disruption of the intestinal microbiome from acute and possibly chronic infection with SARS-CoV-2.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 virus has been found in human adipose tissue.

claim: Two cellular targets of SARS-CoV-2 infection in adipose tissue are mature adipocytes and macrophages.
source: Martinez-Colon et al. identified two cellular targets of SARS-CoV-2 infection in adipose tissue mature adipocytes in adipose depots and macrophages.
evidence: Based on research by Martinez-Colon et al.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 was found in at least one adipose tissue depot in 10 of 18 male individuals in an autopsy series.
source: SARS-CoV-2 was found in at least one adipose tissue depot in 10 of the 18 male individuals (Zickler et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zickler et al., 2022 with autopsy data

claim: The virus was found only in adipose tissue of male individuals who were overweight (BMI >25) or obese.
source: Yet, the virus was found only in adipose tissue of the male individuals who were overweight (BMI >25) or obese (Zickler et al., 2022).

claim: Adipose tissue macrophage infection is largely restricted to a highly inflammatory subpopulation of macrophages that is further activated in response to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: On the other hand, adipose tissue macrophage infection is largely restricted to a highly inflammatory subpopulation of macrophages, present at baseline, that is further activated in response to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
evidence: Based on research findings about macrophage infection

claim: Preadipocytes, while not infected, adopt a proinflammatory phenotype during SARS-CoV-2 infection.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 RNA is detectable in adipocytes in COVID-19 autopsy cases and is associated with an inflammatory infiltrate.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 suppresses de novo lipogenesis as well as adiponectin and adipsin expression in mature adipocytes.

evidence: Supported by citations to Reiterer et al., 2021; Zickler et al., 2022
